stages.summary: The default failed save: the page in a web view and its URL.
A rescue running: the page dimmed under a progress bar. Frozen mid-run — the card polls its state provider and this one never moves.
Mid-transfer at 45%: the embedded glass status bar with its horizon progress.
A download that failed: red status, no progress, and the download glyph back for a retry.
The transfer done and the file saved.
The page held no media this app could recognise.
Saved but not downloaded: the download glyph, no status bar.
Finding the asset behind the post. A message but no percentage — a fraction is only honest once bytes are moving.
Deferred by the Wi-Fi-only policy — status, no percentage, and the transfer resumes the instant Wi-Fi returns.
The share/action extension's failure card, hosted in-app because a simulator cannot drive the real share sheet.
What a single-content app shows when a foreign kind arrives — the same card from every surface.
An article that arrived by email from a contact — the sender attribution on the card.
A save opened and left a third of the way in: the progress the card carries back.
A save whose content download has not finished. Frozen: staged mode suppresses the launch re-ingest, so the spinner stays.
A hard-paywalled save: the locked overlay over the card, with no extracted text behind it.
Onboarding answered, nothing saved yet — the util card in its completed layout is the only card.
A save that never resolved: the error card with its red rim, centred because it is the newest.
Nothing saved and onboarding unanswered: the surface headline, the corona, and the setup block on the util card.
The media deck with nothing in it.
A downloaded image beside an undownloaded video — the two shapes a media card takes.
One save of every kind this app shows; the newest is centred and the util card sits one page left.
A drop past the alert threshold, unacknowledged: the badged card that floats to the top of the whole list.
What a save-time fan-out leaves behind: six retailers, the cheapest tinted, and a seller list taller than its viewport.
The price deck with nothing tracked.
A tracker saved but not yet priced — what the card shows before the first refresh lands.
A tracker whose price has not moved: the product card with a flat series and no alert.
The util card carrying a live weekly pick — the ribbon, the row, and its save affordance.
The save conversation from its first bubble through the Action Button ripple, the Dynamic Island shortcut run, and the real share surface resolving in the sheet.
The mock browser from its first frame: this app's demonstration runs, and the lesson settles on the shared setup popup above it, looping underneath until it is answered.

The lesson as the util card enters it, host and all. In central Luna that is the three sibling lessons in rank order, and the shared setup popup that comes up once the first full cycle is done — the lessons keep replaying underneath it.
The browser step with its cover lifted: the page is asking the user something, which is the one state a plugin's page is on screen.
The one screen a plugin is imported through: what it declares, each capability in plain language, and the containment sentence.
The 'Paste source' leg of the Add button: a bare text view and Import.
The card face of a save a plugin parked while it waits for a browser step — the same lock every kind wears.
One plugin's settings screen: every field type the schema supports, a stopped status with Re-enable, and Delete for an imported plugin.
Settings → Plugins with nothing installed: the empty row and the Add button.
Three installed plugins: one enabled, one disabled, and one the runtime stopped after repeated timeouts.
The full editor over a tracker past its threshold: graph, threshold line, seller list.
The same six retailers in the editor: the list scrolls, and the cut lands mid-row rather than just past the first one.
The chrome a save-time editor wears in the app: the header's back chevron, and no floating exit.
The extension-hosted editor: no back chevron, the floating glass exit standing the seller list up, and a marketplace title trimmed to its product name with the rest kept underneath.
A second store for a product already tracked: the added seller flashes green in the list.
No threshold yet: the alert row parked and dimmed behind its 'Set price alert' button, and no line on the graph.
Axes before enough samples exist to draw a price history.
A week of samples under a threshold line — the shape a drop makes.
A 25%-off threshold committed: accent track and the price it resolves to, on one line.
The row before an alert is set: track dimmed, and a Set price alert button where the threshold price goes.
The same bar paused, at double rate, with autoplay off.
The bar over a reader, mid-article, autoplay on.
The slimmed bar it wears when the reader it is playing is already on screen and can carry the controls itself.
Between articles: the bar announcing what autoplay is about to start.
Highlight mode — the line-at-a-time guide over the same text.
The reader as it appears inside a card: controls in an inline header with a provenance subtitle rather than a nav bar.
A link tapped inside the reader, opening as a second card cut into the page (`claudedocs/readers.md`). Animated, unlike every other stage: the transition IS the subject.
The silent speed reader, one word at a focal point.
The scrolling reader over the fixture article.
Night vs predawn. Both are night; predawn is the same sky lifted one notch (`claudedocs/visual-effects.md`).
Autoplay, on-device trimming, and voice installation.
Which capture sources forward automatically to a destination.
The five-tap screen. Reachable by argument here because five taps in blank space is not a thing a capture script should be doing.
Auto-download, Wi-Fi-only, and save-to-Photos.
An account in good standing: address, inbox filter, sign out.
A sign-in attempt in flight — the spinner in the Connect row. Frozen: staged mode holds the busy flag rather than running a login.
The account the provider stopped accepting: the issue row, the reconnect affordance, and the 'sign in required' detail.
The OAuth variant of the same recovery — an Outlook grant that aged out rather than a password that was refused.
No account: the Sharing Account section IS the sign-in form (`claudedocs/email-login.md`).
Export counts read from the seeded store.
The sheet a picked link-list file produces. Staged with a fixture document — a simulator has no document picker result to hand it.
Send-to-Kindle, reachable only once an account exists.
Font, depth, accent, speed — the reader's own preferences.
The app's own settings list — the categories differ per app.
The same screen on hardware that cannot run the shortcut: renamed, with the shortcut, On-Screen URLs and Double Save sections gone.
The full screen, forced into the Action-Button-capable layout a simulator would otherwise hide.
What a saved post shows in the share/action extension before any download starts. Hosted in-app — a simulator cannot drive the share sheet.
The share/action extension's reader, hosted in-app — the real share sheet cannot be driven on a simulator.
The Contacts list on a device with no contacts yet — its own identity QR and the invite affordance.
What 'send this save to someone' opens, before any contact exists.
After both lessons: the paste row plus matching Safari-history URLs where the setup controls were.
The inline "Store files" line above the setup buttons, on a completed card whose recents it stands down. Only the two apps that download can offer it.
Three saves old enough to earn the email offer, with no account connected — the third setup slot in use.
Headline, corona and setup block, before either lesson is answered.
The same row past the nine-day mark, where the label flips from week to month.
A pick two days old: the week-tier label and the ribbon.
